title: The Bletchley Declaration
subtitle: by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023

authors.name: Governments at the AI Safety Summit

pitch: The first statement signed by the US, China, the EU and 26 others that frontier AI could cause serious, even catastrophic, harm and that the risks need international cooperation.

chapters.g: AI's great potential, alongside risks in daily life and at the frontier.
Particular safety risks from highly capable general-purpose models, including misuse and loss of control.
Why the risks are international and need shared work.
Identifying shared risks and building risk-based policies in each country.
The countries that signed, plus New Zealand which joined in October 2024.

ideas: Frontier AI risks are recognised by rival powers together.
Developers of frontier AI carry strong responsibility for safety.
Summits started a series of meetings and safety institutes.

args.a: A shared statement by rivals is a real step forward.
args.c: Critics note it has no binding commitments.

args.a: Focusing on frontier AI is right.
args.c: Others wanted more on present harms and civil society voices.

questions: Why does it matter that China and the US both signed?
What should a binding follow up include?
Which sentence of the declaration matters most to you?

quiz.w: Where codebreakers worked in the Second World War.
